documented_semantics: disrupted_sympathy_retention is documented as the fraction of disrupted membership retained as latent sympathy rather than erased from the social state.
observed_implementation: Membership assignment writes rebel_sympathy equal to the armed membership fraction and insurgent_affinity equal to that fraction.
Underground disruption computes retained_sympathy = prior_armed_fraction * disrupted_sympathy_retention.
It then writes rebel_sympathy = max(existing_rebel_sympathy, retained_sympathy) and likewise maxes insurgent_affinity.
For a member whose existing sympathy/affinity already equals the prior armed fraction, any retention value <= 1 therefore cannot lower those continuous fields.
A fully disrupted armed participant is changed to the discrete insurgent-sympathy public behavior, whose social signal is 0.7 independent of disrupted_sympathy_retention.

targeted_test.method: Two exact clones of an armed insurgent member were fully disrupted with disrupted_sympathy_retention set to 0 and 1 respectively. The intended-semantics assertion required lower post-disruption rebel_sympathy and insurgent_affinity under retention=0.
targeted_test.failure: retention=0 and retention=1 left identical rebel_sympathy; the first intended-semantics assertion failed.
targeted_test.test_disposition: The temporary failing characterization test was removed after diagnosis so the committed test suite remains green.

implication: The retention parameter acts as a floor rather than a retained fraction in the tested one-insurgent membership path and does not control post-disruption continuous sympathy as documented.
decision: Do not silently correct the mechanism inside the current evidence stream. Treat existing COIN findings as properties of the implemented model; any semantic correction requires a separately versioned mechanism change followed by re-running affected experiments.
